The Medicaid double-dipping scandal exposes systemic failure—2.8 million enrollees gaming multiple state programs, burning $14B annually. This isn’t just waste; it’s a structural collapse of accountability. The Health Care Fairness for All Act (H.R. 3080) tried to fix this by mandating risk adjustment mechanisms and state-level audits, but D.C. bureaucrats ignored its Medicaid payment reforms (Title IV). Washington State’s $8.6M duplicate premium hemorrhage proves the point: without aggressive data cross-checks and eligibility verification, states become ATMs for fraud.

CMS’s 2025 report confirms what watchdogs already knew: overlapping enrollments thrive where oversight dies. The solution isn’t more funding—it’s ruthless efficiency. Track beneficiaries like private insurers track claims. End interstate enrollment loopholes. And audit every dollar before it’s looted.
